title: Chapter 4 – Types of Tournaments: Mock Exam

questions.text: In which tournament system does each player meet every other player exactly once?

options.text: Swiss System
Round Robin
Knock-out
Scheveningen System

questions.explanation: As per Article 4.1, in a Round Robin tournament each player meets every other player once (single round robin) or twice (double round robin). It is considered the fairest tournament system.

questions.text: Which table is used for scheduling pairings in a Round Robin tournament?

options.text: Dutch Table
Buchholz Table
Berger Table
Sonneborn-Berger Table

questions.explanation: As per Article 4.1, the Berger table is used for scheduling pairings in a Round Robin tournament. It ensures a systematic and fair rotation of opponents and colours.

questions.text: In the Swiss System, when is a player eliminated from the tournament?

options.text: After losing two games
After losing one match
Players are never eliminated in a Swiss System
After scoring 0 points in three consecutive rounds

questions.explanation: As per Article 4.2, no player is eliminated in a Swiss system tournament. All players continue to play for the full number of rounds, being paired against opponents with similar scores.

questions.text: In the Scheveningen system, who plays against whom?

options.text: Each player plays every other player in the same team
Each member of one team plays each member of the other team
Players are randomly paired each round
Only the top-ranked players from each team play each other

questions.explanation: As per Article 4.3, in the Scheveningen system, two teams play each other with each member of one team playing each member of the other team. Total games equal the product of the team sizes.

questions.text: In an Armageddon play-off game, what is the result if the game is drawn?

options.text: White wins because White had less time
The game is replayed with reversed colours
Black wins because a draw counts as a win for Black
Both players are eliminated

questions.explanation: As per Article 4.6, in an Armageddon game White has more time but must win. A draw counts as a win for Black. This ensures there is always a decisive result in a play-off.

questions.text: What is the Skalitzka (or Schiller) system?

options.text: A variant of the Round Robin where each player has a fixed opponent
A team tournament where players are arranged in boards 1 to N and play the corresponding board of the opponent team
A knock-out tournament where the loser is eliminated immediately
A Swiss tournament variant used only for national championships

questions.explanation: Per Article 4.4, the Skalitzka system (also called Schiller) is a team tournament format where players are arranged by board order and each player plays the corresponding board from the opposing team.

questions.text: How many rounds are required for a single Round Robin tournament with 8 players?

options.text: 5 rounds
7 rounds
8 rounds
14 rounds

questions.explanation: Per Article 4.1, in a single Round Robin with N players, the number of rounds = N-1 if N is even. With 8 players: 8 - 1 = 7 rounds. Each player plays exactly once against every other player.

questions.text: In a knock-out tournament, what happens to a player who loses their match?

options.text: They are re-seeded into a lower bracket
They play in a consolation bracket
They are eliminated from the tournament
They play a third game to decide placement

questions.explanation: Per Article 4.5, in a knock-out tournament (also called elimination tournament), the loser of each match is eliminated. Only the winner advances to the next round. This continues until one player or team wins the final.

questions.text: Which tournament format is best suited for selecting a single champion from a large field of players?

options.text: Round Robin, because every player plays every other
Swiss System, because no player is eliminated and the highest scorer wins
Scheveningen, because teams compete head-to-head
Matches only, because two players play a fixed number of games

questions.explanation: Per Article 4.2, the Swiss system is best suited for large fields because no player is eliminated, all players complete the same number of rounds, and the player with the highest final score is the winner.

questions.text: In a match (as opposed to a tournament), how is the result typically decided?

options.text: By the total number of wins only, ignoring draws
By the score accumulated over a fixed number of games, with play-offs if tied
By the player who wins the most consecutive games
Always by Armageddon regardless of prior scores

questions.explanation: Per Article 4.7, a match is decided by the total score over a fixed number of games. If tied after the fixed games, tie-break methods specified in advance (such as rapid or Armageddon) determine the winner.
